title: Inverse image of a set-valued constant etale sheaf is constant
statement: Let $v:V\to U$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $E$ be a set. For a scheme $T$ let $\underline E_T$ be the constant sheaf of sets with value $E$ on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], a sheaf of sets on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], and for $e\in E$ let $\eta_T(e)\in\underline E_T(T)$ be the image of $e$ under the canonical map $\eta$ from the constant presheaf $W\mapsto E$ to $\underline E_T$. Let $v^{-1}$ be the etale inverse image of sheaves of sets along $v$ and, for a sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $U_{\Et}$, an object $W$ of $U_{\Et}$ and $s\in\mathcal G(W)$, let $v^*s\in(v^{-1}\mathcal G)(W\times_UV)$ be the pullback of $s$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]; identify $U\times_UV$ with $V$. Then there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of sets $\gamma_v:v^{-1}\underline E_U\to\underline E_V$ on $V_{\Et}$ with $\gamma_v(v^*\eta_U(e))=\eta_V(e)$ for every $e\in E$, and $\gamma_v$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Section 18.43 (Tag 093I, sites-modules-section-constant) and Lemma 093R (sites-modules-lemma-pullback-locally-constant), whose omitted proof is this identification; with Sites, Example 0H7J (sites-example-constant-sheaf), the universal property of the constant sheaf, and the adjunction $v^{-1}\dashv v_*$

proof.text: Apply [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable] with $U$ and $E$. It gives an isomorphism $\underline E_U\cong h_{U_E}$ carrying each canonical section $\eta_U(e)$ to the section represented by the coprojection $\iota_e:U\to U_E$.

source.place: Remark Tag 03P5 and the representability identification used in Lemma Tag 093R

proof.text: The codiagonal $\pi:U_E\to U$ is etale, so $(U_E,\pi)$ is an object of $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and each coprojection $\iota_e:U\to U_E$, which satisfies $\pi\circ\iota_e=\mathrm{id}_U$, is a morphism of $U_{\Et}$: by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] the open subschemes $\iota_e(U)$ cover $U_E$ and $\iota_e$ is an isomorphism onto $\iota_e(U)$, so the restriction of $\pi$ to $\iota_e(U)$ is the inverse isomorphism, hence etale; and being etale is a condition at each point of the source (Morphisms, Definition in Section Tag 02GH). This is the hypothesis `$V$ an object of $Y_{\Et}$' needed to apply [lem-galois-inverse-image-representable] to $U_E$ and its naturality to the $\iota_e$ in the next step.

source.place: Section 29.36 (Tag 02GH), definition of etale morphisms, with Lemma morphisms-lemma-open-immersion-etale

proof.text: By [lem-galois-inverse-image-representable] there is a natural isomorphism $v^{-1}h_{U_E}\cong h_{V\times_UU_E}$, and it carries the pullback of the section represented by $\iota_e$ to the section represented by the base-changed morphism $V\to V\times_UU_E$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03Q1 (4), with Sites Lemma Tag 03CB for the unit-compatible pullback notation

proof.text: The new base-change node [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-base-change] identifies $V\times_UU_E$ with $V_E$, compatibly with every coprojection. Composing the isomorphisms of the preceding steps with the inverse of [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable] for $V$ therefore defines a morphism $\gamma_v:v^{-1}\underline E_U\to\underline E_V$ and gives $\gamma_v(v^*\eta_U(e))=\eta_V(e)$ for every $e$.

source.place: Lemmas Tags 01JB and 01JC after base change, together with the construction in Lemma Tag 093R

proof.text: The morphism is an isomorphism because each factor used to define it is an isomorphism. It is unique with the displayed equations: after the representable identifications, those equations prescribe the images of the canonical coprojection sections, and [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable] gives the sheafification universal property, so two such sheaf morphisms agree.
